findings.highlight: Maybe I’ve grown so accustomed to it after a year that I’ve forgot how important it was.
findings.evidenceJa: この一年それが当たり前になっていて、大切なコトが薄れかけていたのか
findings.governingReading: After a year of taking Sakura’s daily care for granted, Shirou wonders whether his sense of its importance had begun to fade.
findings.explanation: The ungrammatical participle obscures a reflective sentence central to his renewed gratitude.

findings.highlight: The girl looks straight at me.
findings.evidenceJa: 帰ったのですね、マスター
findings.governingReading: Saber simply acknowledges his return and addresses him as Master.
findings.explanation: The English inserts an unsupported gaze action into the first beat of the encounter.

findings.highlight: All sense of reality crumbles on me.
findings.evidenceJa: 現実感というものが、キレイさっぱり崩れてしまった
findings.governingReading: For an instant, Shirou’s sense of reality collapses completely.
findings.explanation: “Crumbles on me” is malformed English and weakens the sudden total collapse conveyed by キレイさっぱり.

findings.highlight: Perhaps the surprise transferred to the girl, as she says this with a bit of surprise.
findings.evidenceJa: 静かな声が自分の名前を呼ぶ
findings.governingReading: Saber calls Shirou’s name quietly, and that restores his sense of reality.
findings.explanation: The English restores an inactive conjecture about surprise transferring to Saber, adding a reaction absent from the active Japanese witness.

findings.highlight: I should move around periodically, or my body will be slow when I will need it the most.
findings.evidenceJa: 定期的に目覚めて体を動かしていなければ、いざという時に動きが鈍ります
findings.governingReading: Saber must wake and move periodically or her movements will be sluggish at the crucial moment.
findings.explanation: The doubled future construction is ungrammatical and makes a precise readiness warning awkward.

findings.highlight: it seems like Saber doesn’t get normal jokes
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーに生半可な冗談は通用しないようだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou concludes that casual or half-measure joking does not work on Saber.
findings.explanation: The English turns this particular mismatch into a broad claim that Saber cannot understand normal jokes, overstating her comic obtuseness.

findings.highlight: The school is a building that can be easily locked up, so it must be an altar chosen as a temple.
findings.evidenceJa: 学校の校舎というものは封鎖しやすい建物ですから、おそらく神殿に見立てた祭壇なのでしょう
findings.governingReading: Because a school building is easy to seal, Saber infers that it is probably an altar fashioned in the likeness of a temple.
findings.explanation: The English tangles the relation between temple and altar and drops Saber’s explicit uncertainty, damaging her technical inference.

findings.highlight: he should be easy to identify since the Master will be lurking at school
findings.evidenceJa: 学校に潜んでいる以上は特定しやすい筈だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou reasons that the Master should be easier to identify if they are hiding at the school.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the unknown Master a male gender that the source withholds.

findings.highlight: Let’s find him somehow and stop the boundary field.
findings.evidenceJa: なんとか見つけだして、結界を止めさせよう
findings.governingReading: Shirou resolves to find the Master and make them stop the bounded field.
findings.explanation: The English makes Shirou and Saber directly stop the field, dropping the source’s causative action against its creator.

findings.highlight: I’ll try to search the school as thoroughly as possible during lunch from tomorrow on
findings.evidenceJa: 明日からはできるだけ昼間のうちに学校を見て回って
findings.governingReading: Starting tomorrow, Shirou plans to inspect the school as much as possible during daylight hours.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the available search period from daytime to lunch, changing his stated plan.
